text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.
GERMANY - German debt and debt futures markets were closed for the Christmas holiday and reopen on Friday.

March Bund futures on Monday ended trade at 100.66, up 23 basis points from Friday's close. The March Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 100.72, up 0.07 from Monday's settlement price.
BRITAIN - Gilt futures ended a half-day's trading slightly higher after global and non-European Union trade data passed without incident.
The futures will trade next on Friday -- another half-day session. The March long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-00/32, up 03/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond futures closed slightly higher after trading in a 16-basis point range, with few operators showing much interest as the London futures market and other major European bourses were closed in the afternoon.
The March notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 128.92, up 0.10 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bond futures traded on the LIFFE market in London closed lower in a thin shortened session ahead of the Christmas break amid continued concern over the lack of progress towards an accord between metalworkers and employers. The lira held fairly steady throughout the morning.
The LIFFE market closed at 1232 GMT and reopens on Friday for another shortened day. The March bond future on LIFFE was trading at 128.30, down 0.20 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were little changed after the store sales report. BTM/Schroders store sales jumped 1.3 percent in the week ended Dec 21. Store sales data in the holiday shopping season is seen as a key reading of consumers' spending power. An abbreviated trading session was set to end at 1900 GMT.
The March Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 113-13/32, down 01/32 from Monday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.59 percent.

JAPAN - Key March Japanese goverment bond futures ended sharply down as market sentiment weakened after the Bank of Japan cut its outright bond purchases on Tuesday morning. Long-liquidation by dealers pushed March further down towards the close.
In after hours trading the March future on LIFFE was trading at 125.67, down 0.48 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
EUROBONDS - The primary market saw no surprises on Christmas Eve with the only activity to surface being the formal launch of a debut 300 million Eurokuna bond by Croatia.
